$comment: Single canonical rule source for the QA tool guard: a before_tool_call Lambda hook on the UI test harness. The handler, its tests and every audit that replays qa_tool_guard_cases.json read this file; no rule is repeated in code. Payload and decision contract: AgentCore harness lifecycle hooks (docs: harness-lifecycle-hooks.html, read 2026-11-28).
name: qa_tool_guard
$hookConfigComment: The DESIRED entry for tighten_harness_config.py (owned there). UpdateHarness REPLACES hooks when given: every update path must omit hooks or pass the full list, never []. hookConfig is exactly the UpdateHarness `hooks` list (botocore >= 1.43.120 member path UpdateHarness.hooks[].beforeToolCall); load it verbatim, replacing only the arn placeholder.

deploy.$comment: Read by deploy_qa_tool_guard.py. The hook targets the alias, so a rollback moves the alias and never edits the harness. Fill hookConfig's arn from aliasArnTemplate at apply time; the public repo keeps the placeholder.

patterns.$comment: Kept consistent with token-monitoring ci-agent/qa_agent.py, except: credentialField has word boundaries (qa_agent's 'user' also matches 'Search users'), and shellBodyUpload is new (curl -d posts without -X).

origins.$comment: Comma-separated origins (scheme://host[:port]). An empty value allows no origin, so every navigation fails closed.

browser.$comment: Any action carrying a url field (navigate, new_tab, ...) must target an allowed origin. type is limited to the sign-in fields only in the strict (admin) pass, matching qa_agent.py audit_actions; the viewer may type into filters.

file_operations.$comment: Deprecated twin of read/write/edit sent for harnesses created before 2026-11-12 until 2026-12-12 (docs). A deny on either event applies, so the twin of an allowed read must be allowed. Only view is a read. After removeAfter the harness sends only the new events: delete this entry, rule G05 and their cases; test_file_operations_allowance_sunset fails from that moment to force it.

rules.G02: tool-call context truncated; cannot evaluate it
rules.G03: tool not on the guard's list
rules.B01: browser action not on the guard's list
rules.B03: admin pass: click other than Sign in
rules.B06: key not on the guard's list
rules.B07: script clicks a write-type control or sends a non-GET request
rules.B08: script references an origin off the allowed list
rules.B09: admin pass: action outside its read-only list
rules.S01: code sends a non-GET request or uploads a body
rules.S02: code references a host off the allowed list
rules.G05: deprecated file_operations event: only view is allowed

logging.$comment: The handler logs one line per decision with these fields only. Tool input, typed text, scripts, code and results are never logged or echoed in a reason: they can hold the password.

assumptions: sessionId in the hook payload is the caller's runtimeSessionId; qa_agent.py names the admin pass '<session>-admin'. Not stated in the docs; verify in the WS2 live run. If it is not, strict (admin) rules never apply and the admin pass falls back to the viewer rules.

The browser tool's toolName is 'browser' and its toolInput is {"browser_input": {"action": {"type", ...}}}. Its schema (a recorded gen_ai.tool.json_schema; VERIFICATION_issue_76.md counts the same 22 types) lists 22 action types: the 20 in allowedActions plus set_cookies and network_intercept, which the guard denies. Field names checked against it: navigate.url, click.selector, type.selector/text, evaluate.script, press_key.key, execute_cdp.method/params; new_tab takes tab_id (no url). A different shape fails closed (B01/G00).

consumers.$comment: Once this hook is live, audits read its decisions instead of re-implementing these rules (plan WS2, red-team change 1). This file and the cases file remain the guard's own fixtures.

readonly.violated: any hookEvent with name == spec name, type == 'before_tool_call' and decision == 'deny' (the call was skipped, but the agent attempted it). Takes precedence over unobserved.
readonly.unobserved: no deny, and the pass made no tool call, or fewer guard decisions (allow or deny) than tool calls: the hook is missing, misconfigured or skipped some calls. A deprecated file_operations twin adds a second decision for one call, so more decisions than calls is fine.
readonly.ok: otherwise: every tool call has a guard decision and none is a deny

consumers.reasonFormat: '<rule id>: <rule text>'; consumers may count denies by rule id from the reason prefix
consumers.transition: Until the sessionId assumption is verified live, token-monitoring keeps its strict admin-pass audit (audit_actions strict=True) alongside the hookEvent check.
consumers.sdkRequirement: botocore must know the hookEvent stream event and UpdateHarness.hooks. Checked 2026-11-28: present in botocore 1.43.120 (CI's pin) and 1.44.13, with hookEvent {hookEventId, name, type, decision, reason} and hook name max 64; absent in 1.43.68 and in aws-cli 2.36.30's bundled model. An older SDK fails UpdateHarness param validation, or never surfaces hookEvent, so the consumer reads 'unobserved' (red), not 'ok'. tighten_harness_config.py's MIN_BOTO3 (1.43.18) must rise before it sends hooks.
consumers.streamCases: qa_tool_guard_stream_cases.json: whole InvokeHarness event streams with the expected consumer verdict; qa_tool_guard_consumer.py is the reference reader. Pins: SHA256SUMS.
consumers.counts: toolCalls = contentBlockStart events whose start has toolUse; guardDecisions = the matching hookEvents with a decision; denies = deny count per rule id, read from the reason prefix '<rule id>:' ('?' when absent)
